root_cause.text: The EIP93 crypto driver’s remove/error-unwind path unregistered every algorithm in `eip93_algs` unconditionally, instead of checking the hardware option register and only unregistering algorithms that were actually registered for the silicon’s supported features.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `eip93_algo_is_supported()` and changes both `eip93_unregister_algs()` and the failure path in `eip93_register_algs()`/`eip93_crypto_remove()` to pass `supported_algo_flags` and skip unsupported algorithms; the CVE description states that “Currently, all algorithms are unregistered, even those not supported by HW. This results in panic on platforms that don't have all options implemented in silicon.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Make algorithm unregistration conditional on hardware-supported crypto features.
intent_record.what: A new helper function, eip93_algo_is_supported(u32 alg_flags, u32 supported_algo_flags), was added to test whether a given algorithm’s flags are compatible with the hardware capability mask. The existing eip93_unregister_algs() function signature was changed to take an additional u32 supported_algo_flags parameter, and its loop now skips unregistering any algorithm whose flags are not supported according to the new helper before entering the unregister switch statement.
intent_record.how: At runtime, unregistering algorithms now becomes capability-aware: only algorithms that match the device’s supported feature flags are passed through the unregister logic, while unsupported ones are ignored. This prevents cleanup from acting on algorithms that should not be considered present for the given hardware configuration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate algorithm capability checks during EIP93 registration and simplify AES keysize handling.
intent_record.what: The per-algorithm support checks in eip93_register_algs() were consolidated into a call to eip93_algo_is_supported(alg_flags, supported_algo_flags). The AES max-key-size handling was also simplified: for non-HMAC AES algorithms, the code now conditionally sets max_keysize to 128, 192, or 256 bits based on individual AES key support flags, and still adds CTR_RFC3686_NONCE_SIZE for RFC3686 modes. Separate hash-support continue checks for MD5, SHA1, SHA224, and SHA256 were removed from this function.
intent_record.how: At runtime, algorithm registration now relies on a centralized capability check instead of several ad hoc conditionals, which should make unsupported algorithms skip registration more consistently. AES cipher registrations continue to advertise the maximum key size supported by the hardware, and RFC3686 AES modes keep the nonce-size adjustment. Hash registration logic is no longer filtered inline here, implying that support gating is handled elsewhere or through the new helper.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the failure cleanup path to pass the supported algorithm flags when unregistering algorithms.
intent_record.what: The call to `eip93_unregister_algs()` in the failure path was changed from passing only `i` to passing `supported_algo_flags` and `i`.
intent_record.how: On registration failure, the cleanup routine now receives the supported algorithm flags in addition to the count/index, allowing it to unregister the correct set of algorithms instead of using insufficient state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the hardware algorithm flags during device removal so only the appropriate EIP93 algorithms are unregistered.
intent_record.what: In eip93_crypto_remove(), a new local u32 variable algo_flags was added, it is initialized by reading the EIP93_REG_PE_OPTION_1 hardware register via readl(), and the call to eip93_unregister_algs() was changed from passing only ARRAY_SIZE(eip93_algs) to passing both algo_flags and ARRAY_SIZE(eip93_algs).
intent_record.how: At remove time, the driver now consults the device's PE_OPTION_1 register to determine the active algorithm flags before unregistering algorithms, so cleanup can be performed in a way that matches the hardware configuration instead of using a fixed unregister path.

grouping_result.intent: Use the hardware algorithm flags during device removal so only the appropriate EIP93 algorithms are unregistered.
Consolidate algorithm capability checks during EIP93 registration and simplify AES keysize handling.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make EIP93 algorithm unregistration conditional on the hardware-supported crypto flags, including in the device removal and failure cleanup paths.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they make EIP93 algorithm unregistration conditional on the hardware-supported crypto flags in both the remove path and failure unwind path, instead of unregistering all algorithms unconditionally.

The change centers on EIP93 registration capability checks, which is directly related to the bug where remove/error-unwind logic failed to match registrations to hardware-supported features. Consolidating capability checks suggests it may affect which algorithms are registered and therefore which ones should be unregistered.

candidates.rationale: The cleanup path unregisters algorithms using only the count of attempted registrations, not the hardware-supported flags. This can cause unregistering algorithms that were never registered on the detected silicon.
The remove path unconditionally unregisters every algorithm in eip93_algs, regardless of which crypto capabilities the hardware actually supports and which algorithms were registered.

vuln_statements.explanation: This remove-path call unregisters all algorithms unconditionally, matching the root cause that the driver failed to check the hardware option register and only unregister algorithms actually registered for the detected silicon.

This cleanup-path call uses only the number of attempted registrations rather than the hardware-supported algorithm flags, so it can unregister algorithms that were never registered on the running hardware.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant remove path is present here: `static void eip93_crypto_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)` calls `eip93_unregister_algs(ARRAY_SIZE(eip93_algs));`, which is an unconditional unregister of the entire `eip93_algs` table. The helper itself also unregisters based only on the passed count: `for (j = 0; j < i; j++) ... crypto_unregister_*(&eip93_algs[j]...)`. However, the root cause says the bug is unregistering every algorithm unconditionally instead of checking the hardware option register and only unregistering algorithms that were actually registered. In this commit, the registration path already filters by `algo_flags` in `eip93_register_algs(...)` using checks like `if (!(supported_algo_flags & EIP93_PE_OPTION_AES)) continue;` and similar for DES/3DES and hashes, so the code shown does not demonstrate the vulnerable construct as an introduced bug here; it is the normal initial implementation. There is also no fix for the reported bug in the remove path, because removal still uses `ARRAY_SIZE(eip93_algs)` and does not track what was registered.
